title: CTV Overtakes Cable in Political Ad Spend for the First Time in a Midterm

facts.fact: According to AdImpact data shared with Adweek, political advertisers had spent $11.4 billion to date in the 2026 midterms cycle, up 28% from the 2022 midterms.
facts.quote: political advertisers have spent $11.4 billion to date, up 28% from the 2022 midterms, according to data shared with ADWEEK from AdImpact

facts.fact: The 2026 midterms cycle has already drawn more ad spend than any election cycle tracked by AdImpact, including the 2024 U.S. presidential cycle, which AdImpact's page says set a previous record of $11.2 billion.
facts.quote: The cycle has already drawn more ad spend than any election cycle tracked by AdImpact, including the 2024 U.S. presidential cycle, which set a previous record of $11.2 billion.

facts.fact: Of the $2.5 billion increase in political ad investment from the 2022 midterms, more than half (53%) went to connected TV.
facts.quote: of the $2.5 billion uptick in investment from the 2022 midterms, more than half (53%) has gone to connected TV

facts.fact: Political ad spend in connected TV (CTV) grew 122%, from roughly $1.1 billion in the 2022 midterms to $2.4 billion in the 2026 cycle.
facts.quote: spend in CTV grew 122%, from roughly $1.1 billion in the 2022 midterms to $2.4

facts.fact: Political ad spend on cable fell 26% compared with the 2022 cycle, to less than $1.3 billion.
facts.quote: cable fell 26% to less than $1.3 billion

facts.fact: The article reports that CTV overtook cable in political ad spend for the first time in a midterm cycle.
